simple.meaning: בֶּצַע (betsaʻ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “plunder ; by extension, gain (usually unjust).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 23 times in Genesis, Exodus, Judges, 1 Samuel, Job, and 8 more, beginning at Genesis 37:26. The surrounding contexts include family, family line, blood, righteousness, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בֶּצַע (H1215) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: בֶּצַע (betsaʻ) / H1215 is traced through Genesis 37:26, Exodus 18:21, Judges 5:19, 1 Samuel 8:3 with source-language evidence and verse context.

timeline.evidenceText: Judah said to his brothers, “What profit is it if we kill our brother and conceal his blood?

Moreover you shall provide out of all the people able men which fear God: men of truth, hating unjust gain; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.
“The kings came and fought,
His sons didn’t walk in his ways, but turned away after dishonest gain, took bribes, and perverted justice.
Is it any pleasure to the Almighty that you are righteous?
Hear, Yahweh, and have mercy on me.
Turn my heart toward your statutes,
So are the ways of everyone who is greedy for gain.
He who is greedy for gain troubles his own house,
A tyrannical ruler lacks judgment.
He who walks righteously
Yes, the dogs are greedy.
I was angry because of the iniquity of his covetousness and struck him.
“For from their least even to their greatest, everyone is given to covetousness.
Therefore I will give their wives to others
But your eyes and your heart are only for your covetousness,
You who dwell on many waters, abundant in treasures,
“ ‘ “Behold, therefore I have struck my hand at your dishonest gain which you have made, and at your blood which has been within you.
Her princes within it are like wolves ravening the prey, to shed blood, and to destroy souls, that they may get dishonest gain.

They come to you as the people come, and they sit before you as my people, and they hear your words, but don’t do them; for with their mouth they show much love, but their heart goes after their gain.

definitions.full: H1215. betsa בֶּ֫צַע noun masculine gain made by violence , unjust gain, profit — בֶּ֫צַע Gen 37:26 7 t. (construct Judg 5:19 +); בָּ֑צַע Exod 18:21 7 t.; suffix בִּצֱע֑ךָ Jer 22:17 ; בִּצְעֵךְ 51:13 ; Ezek 22:13 ; בִּצְעוֺ Isa 56:11 ; 57:17 ; בִּצְעָם Ezek 33:31 ; Micah 4:13 ; — gain made by violence (nearly = plunder) Judg 5:19 ; Micah 4:13 ; more Generally, unjust gain Exod 18:21 ; 1Sam 8:3 ; Psa 119:36 ; Prov 28:16 ; Isa 33:15 ; 56:11 ; 57:17 ; Jer 22:17 ; 51:13 ; Ezek 22:13 ; 33:21 ; as accusative of congnate meaning with verb with בָּצַע Prov 1:19 ; 15:27 ; Jer 6:13 ; 8:10 ; Ezek 22:27 ; Hab 2:9 ; profit (with selfish suggestion) ׳מהבֿ Gen 37:26 ; Mal 3:14 compare Psa 30:10 ; Job 22:3 .
